issues.description: The type of the StockIngredient.price field (and its constructor/getter) is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement UML specifies price as int, the template implementation defines price as double, while the solution uses int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected type and leads to inconsistent method signatures (constructor/getter) they must call/use when implementing SealSaloon methods like calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the type of StockIngredient.price across all artifacts. Prefer changing the template to use int for price (field, constructor parameter, and getPrice return type) to match the UML and the solution, or alternatively update the problem statement and solution to use double if fractional prices are intended. Ensure constructor and getter signatures are updated consistently.
